tranches.title: Leaves
tranches.about: Files with no dependency on any other LurkerKit type.

tranches.title: Core entities
tranches.about: Buffers, messages, networks and what hangs directly off them.

tranches.title: Ignores, commands, message rows
tranches.about: The pure logic layered on the entities: what is hidden, what a slash command means, what the message list draws.

tranches.title: Wire
tranches.about: Frames and the parser that produces them.

tranches.title: Store
tranches.about: `ChatState` and the reducer. The prototype's store in `:app` stays until T7 retires it; the two coexist meanwhile.

tranches.title: Client
tranches.about: REST + WebSocket over OkHttp. Replaces `:app`'s prototype client.

tranches.title: Session
tranches.about: The view model the UI talks to, and what it persists.

tranches.title: Sync to lurker-ios 63255a5
tranches.about: Drift after the port: per-network away (lurker#994, lurker-ios#193) and upload limits + the pre-shrink rule (lurker-ios#155, #194).

notes.Client/JSON.swift: → `client/Json.kt`. `FailableDecodable` is `Json.decodeEach`. The reads bridge numbers and booleans the way `NSNumber` does.
notes.Model/ISOTime.swift: One ISO parser covers both of LurkerKit's; no lock.
notes.Client/OAuth.swift: An `object`. `Registration`/`Callback`/`TokenGrant` are sealed interfaces (payloads named `message`, `code`, `token`); `PKCE` a data class over `MessageDigest` + `SecureRandom`. `callback` reads the query by hand (`support.removingPercentEncoding`, shared with `PreviewSelection`; the fragment is found first, so a `?` inside it opens no query) so `+` stays `+` and `%2B` decodes to `+`, as `URLComponents` does. JSON bodies read through `FrameParser.jsonObject(data)`.
notes.Session/SessionStore.swift: Keychain → `SecureStorage` (`read`/`write`/`delete` by account; implementations never throw), implemented by `:app` over the Keystore — readable after first unlock, excluded from backup and transfer, as the Swift’s accessibility attribute asked. `account`/`legacyAccount` keep their values; `service` has no counterpart. `save` is one replacing `write`. `SessionCodec` is kotlinx with `ignoreUnknownKeys`. Port-only: `PendingSignIn` and its save/take/clear under account `pending-sign-in` — the sign-in out in the browser, so a redirect that outlives the process can finish (`ChatViewModel.resumeSignIn`); iOS needs none, its sheet dies with the app.
notes.Session/OAuthClients.swift: `UserDefaults` → the kit’s `DefaultsStorage` (shared with `SettingsCache`); the client ids travel as a `JsonObject` of strings, read all-or-nothing. `key` keeps its value and must survive sign-out.
notes.Store/SettingsCache.swift: `UserDefaults` → `DefaultsStorage` (`dictionary`, `set`, `removeObject`, mirroring the three calls), implemented by `:app`; no default storage. Values travel as `JsonObject`.
notes.Client/Uploads.swift: `UploadProgressDelegate` keeps its name and whole-percent coalescing; `UploadProgressBody` is the counting OkHttp `RequestBody` (a `ForwardingSink`) that feeds it. `upload` streams the already-assembled multipart file, as the Swift does. `assemble` deletes its partial file on failure, which LurkerKit leaves to iOS. `UploadLimits.maxUploadBytes` is `Long` (a byte count).
notes.Model/Typing.swift: `OutgoingTyping` is a mutable class (PORTING.md, structs that mutate, case 3). Composing is judged on the trimmed draft and a `//`-escaped line counts as a message (lurker-ios#202).
notes.Model/UploadContentTypes.swift: `[UTType]` → MIME patterns. Adds `application/json`, which `text/*` cannot reach and `.text` does by conformance.
notes.Model/ServerAddress.swift: Parses by hand to match `URLComponents`, then also requires that OkHttp can load the address — stricter than iOS at a few edges, pinned by a port-only test.
notes.Model/NetworkAbbreviation.swift: Grows by code point where Swift grows by grapheme cluster; differs only for names with combining marks.
notes.Commands/SpoilerMarkup.swift: Checked against the Swift over a corpus; differs only when a combining mark follows a `|`.
notes.Rendering/NickColor.swift: `lowercasedLikeTheWeb` is written out (Final_Sigma with case-ignorable skipping), not `lowercase()`, whose JDK rule disagreed with node on 204 of 6,026 random strings; the port agrees on all but 8 (U+10D4E, unassigned in JDK 21's Unicode). Case_Ignorable comes from Java's general categories plus a Word_Break list, so it follows the runtime's Unicode version. `trimForColor` walks code points.
notes.Rendering/NickHighlighter.swift: Case-insensitive matching of non-ASCII nicks is engine-dependent; verify on a device.
notes.Rendering/URLMatcher.swift: A word boundary beside a combining mark is engine-dependent; verify on a device.
notes.Rendering/IRCFormatting.swift: `rawIndex` is tested from `RelayEnvelopeTests` (T3); checked against the Swift meanwhile.
notes.Client/NotificationTap.swift: Input is a `Map<String, Any?>`; FCM's all-strings data map is the shape Android will hand it.
notes.Model/Settings.swift: `SettingValue.Int` is 32-bit; a wire number past that is skipped rather than wrapped.
notes.Model/ChannelModes.swift: Complete with T5: `channelAccess` is an extension on `ChatState`. `topicSetterLine` takes the date formatter from the app. `ChannelRefusals` and `ChannelModeDrafts` compare all their state, not just what is on screen.
notes.Model/Replies.swift: `shown` returns `Replies.Shown(quote, text)` for the named tuple.
notes.Model/Reactions.swift: Grapheme counting through `BreakIterator`: matches Swift on JDK 21 for emoji sequences, not for Indic conjuncts; verify on a device.
notes.Model/Buffer.swift: `BufferKey.id` folds with `lowercase()`, which applies final sigma where Swift does not.
notes.Model/BufferOrder.swift: `localizedCaseInsensitiveCompare` → `java.text.Collator`. The host JDK orders punctuation differently from ICU; verify on a device.
notes.Model/SearchRequest.swift: The query is encoded by `support.percentEncodedQuery`, to `URLComponents`' rule.
notes.Model/LinkPreview.swift: `isViewable` parses with `HttpUrl`, which can read a different host than Foundation when a backslash sits in the authority: the player must be handed `HttpUrl.toString()`, never the raw string (T6). Numeric fields decode slightly more strictly than `JSONDecoder`.
notes.Model/NetworkPreset.swift: The catalogue is a byte-for-byte copy of LurkerKit's, itself a copy of the web's.
notes.Model/PendingJoins.swift: A mutable class (case 3). `stopOpening` rewrites each immutable `Request` through `setValue`, keeping the order.
notes.Model/UnsentCorrelator.swift: A mutable class (case 3). Mints `android-N` client ids where LurkerKit mints `ios-N`.
notes.Model/HighlightGrouping.swift: "The day before" is ported from ICU's wall-time rule, not `minusDays`; Yesterday is a same-calendar-day check (lurker-ios#200), matched against the Swift for every day 2000–2030 in all 443 zones. Depends on time-zone data; verify on a device.
notes.Model/MessageActions.swift: `MessageAction.symbol` keeps the SF Symbol names; the app maps them to its own icons.
notes.Model/WhoisResult.swift: A plain value; the string-or-number reading is FrameParser's (T4).
notes.Model/Modes.swift: No Swift test of its own; checked against the Swift over a corpus.
notes.Model/UploadsRequest.swift: The query is encoded by `support.percentEncodedQuery`, to `URLComponents`' rule.
notes.Model/NetworkProxy.swift: `ProxyDraft` is a plain class edited through `setType` and `edited`, so the protocol cannot change without its port.
notes.Model/IgnoreRule.swift: `summary` takes the expiry formatter from the app; the private `ExpiryText` is not ported.
notes.Model/IgnoreMatch.swift: Literal masks compare through `FoldedLiteral`, not `equals(ignoreCase)`. Case-insensitive matching of non-ASCII is engine-dependent; verify on a device.
notes.Model/IgnoreSet.swift: Value equality over the rules, where LurkerKit's class has identity.
notes.Commands/IgnoreArgs.swift: `parse` returns `support.Result`. The pattern length limit counts UTF-16 units, the server's own rule, as LurkerKit now does too (lurker-ios#198).
notes.Model/RelayEnvelope.swift: `RelayTemplate` is a plain class (it holds a compiled regex). `.` is spelled out so the host JVM stops where ICU does.
notes.Model/RelayBotSet.swift: Value equality, where LurkerKit's class has identity.
notes.Model/PreviewText.swift: `stripHiddenUrls` takes an `AttributedBody` interface for `:app` to implement, where LurkerKit takes an `NSMutableAttributedString`.
notes.Model/Consolidation.swift: Returns structure, not sentences: the wording is the app's renderer's.
notes.Model/MessageRows.swift: `AwayDivider`'s reason is `awayMessage`. Day boundaries depend on time-zone data; verify on a device.
notes.Commands/CommandParser.swift: `parse` takes the app's date formatter, for the `/ignore` listing. Lines are cut by UTF-16 unit; differs from Swift only where a combining mark follows a slash, a space or a sigil. `argLine` and `body()` trim newlines too (lurker-ios#197). `awayFlag` (lurker#994): a space wearing a combining mark leaves the mark behind here, where Swift drops it with the separator — Port note + port-only test.
notes.Commands/Command.swift: `CommandEffect` is a sealed interface of 23 cases in Swift order.
notes.Model/NickCompletion.swift: `spokenPunctuation` and `isMarkScalar` read the JDK's Unicode tables; verify on a device.
notes.Model/PreviewSelection.swift: `looksLikeMedia` reads the path by hand to Foundation's rules rather than through `HttpUrl`; pinned by a port-only test.
notes.Model/AwayStrip.swift: Chooses how much of the date to show (`Since`, carrying the ICU skeleton); the app formats it. "This year" is the ISO year, where LurkerKit asks the user's calendar.
notes.Client/ServerFrame.swift: `ServerFrame` is a sealed interface of 50 cases, Swift order. Three cases share a name with a model type (`AwayState`, `WhoisResult`, `ModeSpec`); the model type is written fully qualified there. Every type is an immutable data class.
notes.Client/FrameParser.swift: Reads through kotlinx.serialization where LurkerKit reads through `JSONSerialization` (behind `JSONTextRepair`); kotlinx’s answer is kept and every difference is pinned port-only in `FrameParserTests` — see `object`’s Port note (PORTING.md, JSON). A lone-surrogate escape reads on both sides, as U+FFFD on iOS and the lone unit here; a leading U+FEFF is kept on both. `jsonObject(data:)` reads UTF-8 only. The parser never throws and bounds nesting at Foundation’s 512 containers (kotlinx would overflow the stack). `channelKeys` and `peerPresence` fold nicks with `lowercase()`, which applies final sigma. `WhoisResult.signedOn` beyond `Instant` is null.
notes.Store/LurkerStore.swift: `ChatState` is an immutable data class (case 2): its thirteen mutators return the updated copy, and it compares all its state. `LurkerStore` publishes through a replaying `SharedFlow` with an unbounded buffer, not a `StateFlow`: `CurrentValueSubject` republishes equal states and a subscriber sees every value in order, and `AppBadge` writes on the settled EDGE of a burst (lurker-ios#134), which a conflating flow would skip. One assignment per method. `clock: () -> Instant` is injected for the tests. Port-only mechanics: `dropBuffers` folds the bulk drops into one subtraction per map; `noteBookmarks` copies the set only on a change; `applyBufferRenamed` is lifted out of `reduce`, body unchanged. `visibleMembers` matches your nick with `IgnoreMatch.FoldedLiteral` in place of `caseInsensitiveCompare`; `typists` tie-breaks by UTF-16 unit, Swift by scalar. ⚠ `ChatState`’s internal fields are settable through the public `copy`; nothing outside the kit should. `ChatState.canWrite` is the one can-it-go-out rule; `canReact` is built on it.
notes.Session/AppBadge.swift: The badge write is an injected `(Int) -> Unit`, as the Swift’s `write` closure. `follow(states: Flow<ChatState>, scope)` collects in the given scope; calling it again cancels the previous collection, as replacing the `AnyCancellable` does. No `[weak self]`.
notes.Client/LurkerClient.swift: `LurkerClient(scope, onFrame, httpClient = bearerOnlyConfiguration(), mediaCacheDirectory = null, ioDispatcher = Dispatchers.IO)`, main-confined. `async` → `suspend`; every `Task {}` from main-confined code → `support.task` (a `launch` that yields first, so a stored `Job` is assigned before its body runs under `Main.immediate`); listener callbacks hop to main with `scope.launch`. One suspending `OkHttpClient.await` over `enqueue`; per-request timeouts travel as a tag; JSON bodies written as bytes so Content-Type is exactly `application/json`. `URLSessionWebSocketTask` → `okhttp3.WebSocket`: first of `onClosing`/`onClosed`/`onFailure` wins; `onClosing` answers `close(1000)`; `.goingAway` → `close(1001)`; stale sockets ignored by identity. `send`: `onComplete` means queued; `onFlush` fires a turn later once `queueSize` drains (`awaitWritten`, 2 s bound) — the nearest OkHttp comes to "written". Reply continuations are resumed a turn later (`resumeLater`), as `CheckedContinuation` does, so a waiter never runs inline in `openSocket`/`close` under `Main.immediate`. The media client has its own `Dispatcher` (the shared five-per-host cap would queue REST and the upgrade behind image bodies); `clearMediaCache` swallows `IOException`. ⚠ Receive has no backpressure; a replaced socket finishes its upgrade before closing. `registerDevice` sends `transport: "fcm"` (server rule). Cleartext refusal has its own user-visible text. `[weak self]` dropped: a cancelled scope stops the work. `playableMediaURL`/`socketURL` return `String?`. Logging via `java.util.logging`. `upload` assembles (and later deletes) the multipart body on `ioDispatcher` (U8), everything else on the caller's thread; `evictAll` stays on the calling thread, and `ChatViewModel` calls it off main. REST bodies read through `FrameParser.jsonObject(data)` (no `JSONTextRepair`). `openBuffer` reports whether it went out (lurker-ios#201). `send` answers OkHttp's `queued`, so a frame it refuses is false at once, where LurkerKit can only learn of it from the write's completion; a refusal raises no "Send failed" (the caller hears the false) (client sweep, lurker-ios#215).
notes.Client/LinkPreviews.swift: `LinkPreviewStore(scope, now = Instant::now, jitter, resolve: suspend (List<String>) -> List<LinkPreview>)`; its tasks go through `support.task`. `retry` is insertion-ordered where Swift’s dictionary is not; the re-ask delay rounds up to the millisecond.
notes.Session/ChatViewModel.swift: `ChatViewModel(scope, sessions, settingsCache, oauthClients, formatExpiry, httpClient = LurkerClient.bearerOnlyConfiguration(), mediaCacheDirectory = null)`, main-confined; the stores have no defaults because each needs platform storage the kit does not have. `sessionSubject`/`statusSubject` are `support.CurrentValueSubject`; `channelEvents` is a `SharedFlow` with an unbounded buffer (its two consumers patch open lists from every live MODE row and a burst lands before a collector runs). Every `Task` → `support.task`; stored ones (`reconnectTask`, `draftFlushes`) → `Job`; `[weak self]` dropped (the scope’s cancellation ends the work). `authorize` is `suspend (HttpUrl) -> String?`. `formatExpiry` is port-only: the kit never formats a date, so the app hands in the ignore-expiry formatter once and `send` passes it to `CommandParser`. `serverSupportsAPNs` checks for `fcm` (the server rule), name kept to grep across repos. `init` sits at the bottom so every property has initialised first. ⚠ Not exercised in Kotlin: `signIn` (needs HTTP), `logout`/`onAuthLost`, the 500 ms draft flush over a live socket, `enterBackground`’s drafts-plus-presence path. `upload` is safe to call from main (the client moves its disk work); `logout`/`onAuthLost` purge the media cache and staged media on `Dispatchers.IO` (`purgeMedia`, U8) — a held Job that `signIn` and `playableMediaURL` join, re-run by a sessionless launch. DMs wait for their row (lurker-ios#201): `openAndShow`/`supersedeLandings`, landings through `onBufferOpened` → the app's `AppEvents`; `openBuffer` returns `Boolean` with an internal `openBufferSeam` for tests; `sendMessageSeam` stands in for a command's PRIVMSG. `sendRawSeam` stands in for a raw line; `noteUnknownCommand` and `rawVerb` are internal for tests. Port-only: `signIn` saves a `PendingSignIn` while the page is up and clears it when the page answers; `resumeSignIn(callback)` finishes from it when the redirect starts a fresh process (ignored unless signed out); the exchange is the shared private `finishSignIn`.
notes.Client/ImageShrink.swift: UTIs → MIME types (PORTING.md): `Source.typeIdentifier` and `Format.typeIdentifier` keep their names and hold MIME strings (`Format.typeIdentifier == Format.mime`); the mapping table, `com.adobe.raw-image` → `image/x-adobe-dng`, is the Port note on `Source.typeIdentifier`. Exact, case-sensitive comparison, as the Swift. The measuring and redraw are app-side (iOS `ImageConverter`; Android U8 fills `Source` from `ImageDecoder`/`BitmapFactory`).
notes.Model/PendingOpen.swift: Was `PendingDccOpen` (lurker-ios#201): DMs and DCC chats share one wait, keyed by `BufferKey`. `PendingOpen` is immutable; its `init(key:now:)` is a companion `invoke` (a second constructor clashes with the private primary one on the JVM). `PendingOpens` is a mutable class (case 3), owned by the view model alone.
notes.Model/FeedPaging.swift: A mutable class (case 3), one owner (the app's `FeedPager`); `items` is replaced, never edited in place, so a snapshot holding an earlier list stays valid. `Fetch`/`Landing` constructors internal. Differentially checked against the Swift over 24,400 random ops: identical. `remove` pages only inside `prefetchWindow` and spends no hop (moved into LurkerKit from the app's old `FeedPager`); the app still keeps a removed row out of a reload already in flight, which LurkerKit lacks.
notes.Client/JSONTextRepair.swift: Not ported: a workaround for Foundation's `JSONSerialization` (it refuses a lone surrogate escape and strips a leading U+FEFF), and kotlinx does neither (PORTING.md, JSON). The one visible difference: a lone surrogate the server sent reads as U+FFFD on iOS and as the lone unit here.
notes.Model/Speakers.swift: Entries keep each nick as last spelled, for nick completion (`recent`, newest first, case-folded tiebreak).

NotificationTapTests.swift.note: Pins what `JSONSerialization` makes of an APNs payload; a push reaches Android as FCM's string map, which the port-only tests cover.

UploadContentTypesTests.swift.note: Extension→MIME lookups are `MimeTypeMap` on Android, invisible to a JVM module; they belong in an instrumented `:app` test. Two more are ported in part: UTI-conformance assertions have no MIME equivalent.

AwayStripTests.swift.note: Three assertions about what `DateFormatter` writes for a template are left to the app's formatter, on a device.

PreviewMediaRequestTests.swift.note: `playableMediaURL` hands the player an `HttpUrl.toString()` (the T2 ruling), which lower-cases the scheme; the test asserts the input comes back verbatim. A port-only test pins that an uppercase scheme is still recognised as absolute.

FrameParserTests.swift.note: Pins `JSONTextRepair`'s U+FFFD, which is not ported; the port-only `testBacklogWithALoneSurrogateKeepsEveryRowAndTheLoneHalf` pins what kotlinx keeps.

PreviewDecodeTests.swift.note: Pins `JSONTextRepair`'s U+FFFD; the port-only `loneSurrogateDoesNotDiscardTheBatchAndKeepsTheLoneHalf` pins what kotlinx keeps.
